Chart system · Concept 03 · White

Instrument

Every chart is a module with the same seven slots, built by one function per chart form, so the next chart comes from the kit. Texture and open marks carry a second code after color, as the atlas’s evidence lines do, and each module works as a still image and as a panel with a Chart and Table switch.

  • NewsprintThe same ten modules on the warm ground.
  • CharcoalTwo modules on the dark ground.
  • Social cardOne module set as a 1080 by 1350 card.
  • SystemThe kit on one sheet, and the full reading guide.

How to read these charts

The full guide

  • Kind and grade. The label over each title names the kind of claim and how sure its evidence is.
  • Title and measure. The title states the finding; the line under it gives what, where and when.
  • Dark and gray. The darkest mark is what the title is about; gray marks are there for comparison.
  • Red. A red mark points at the one thing the title names; it never marks a party or a side.
  • Check it. Every chart has a Table button, notes and a source line.

Studio note for reviewers

S01 · Big number in context

Reader question. Do Republicans and Democrats agree on anything about Congress?

Why this form. A big number answers yes at a glance; the party bars beside it show the two figures one point apart, and the votes show what Congress did three years later.

Kit. register_chart(‘S01’, gen=big_number, adapter=spec_s01). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S02 · Line with event notes

Reader question. What happened to child poverty when the expanded child tax credit was paid, and after it lapsed?

Why this form. A line shows the fall to 2021 and the climb back; the official measure in gray shows what the supplemental measure counts, and the breaks show where the Census Bureau changed its method.

Kit. register_chart(‘S02’, gen=line_events, adapter=spec_s02). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S03 · Ranked bar

Reader question. Who changed the rules: voters, courts or legislatures?

Why this form. Seven instruments ranked by count answer who made the most changes; splitting each bar by the atlas’s direction code shows which way each instrument moved the rules.

Kit. register_chart(‘S03’, gen=ranked_bar, adapter=spec_s03). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S04 · Dot plot or dumbbell

Reader question. Which age groups vote, and did that change between two elections?

Why this form. Two dots per age group show the level and the change at once; printed values and the change in words carry the numbers without a grid.

Kit. register_chart(‘S04’, gen=dumbbell, adapter=spec_s04). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S05 · Small multiples

Reader question. How far apart are homeownership rates by race, and has the gap closed?

Why this form. One panel per group on one scale lets a reader compare each group with the other three, which sit behind it in gray.

Kit. register_chart(‘S05’, gen=small_multiples, adapter=spec_s05). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S06 · Comparison table

Reader question. If a reform path were followed, which way would each outcome move?

Why this form. A table keeps the atlas’s words in every cell; a boxed arrow and a tint let a reader scan the moves across eight rows, and the arrow alone carries each move on a black-and-white copy.

Kit. register_chart(‘S06’, gen=comparison_table, adapter=spec_s06). Column module, 866 px; one HTML table that reflows under 640 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S07 · Map

Reader question. Where can a city adopt ranked-choice voting, and where has the state ruled it out?

Why this form. Equal tiles give every state the same weight and room for its code and the year of its ban; true shapes would hide the small eastern states.

Kit. register_chart(‘S07’, gen=tile_map, adapter=spec_s07). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S08 · Unit chart

Reader question. Have the rules been moving toward voters or away from them?

Why this form. One square per record lets a reader count every change; rows by direction show the whole log at once, with no period chosen for them.

Kit. register_chart(‘S08’, gen=unit_ledger, adapter=spec_s08). Column module, 866 px; one HTML grid of 24 px units that reflows.

Studio note for reviewers

S09 · Timeline

Reader question. Which rule changes since 1870 decided who counts, who governs, who owns and who checks?

Why this form. Four lanes on one true time scale show when each thread changed; the register under the drawing names every event and what it did, in date order.

Kit. register_chart(‘S09’, gen=strip_timeline, adapter=spec_s09). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Studio note for reviewers

S10 · Evidence mix

Reader question. How much of each everyday answer rests on documented fact?

Why this form. A 100% bar per question compares the mix across questions of different sizes; sorting by the documented share puts the firmest answers first, and the count beside each share shows its base.

Kit. register_chart(‘S10’, gen=share_bars, adapter=spec_s10). Column module, 866 px; artboards 866, 560, 358 and 328 px.

Chart system · Concept 03 · Charcoal

Two modules on Charcoal

On Charcoal, Newsprint carries the named series, Dim Newsprint the context, and texture still carries the evidence grade. Text from 13 to 15 px sets one weight heavier. Lifted Prussian and lifted Verdigris sit only 0.022 apart in lightness here, so dark charts keep to two inks and label every mark.

  • Named series and away from voters. Newsprint, #DCD9D2, 13.29:1
  • Context and secondary text. Dim Newsprint, #A3A19C, 7.26:1
  • Toward voters. Verdigris, 30% toward Newsprint, #76978F, 5.88:1
  • Middle level. Stone, 35% toward Newsprint, #878A8F, 5.41:1
  • Plausible fill. Stone, #5D636D, 3.10:1
  • Gridline, decorative. Stone, 45% toward Charcoal, #393C41, 1.69:1

Chart system · Concept 03 · Social card

S01 as a 1080 by 1350 card

The card is the S01 module with its controls removed. big_number() draws a 600 px artboard and the card sets it at 1.34 times, so the smallest chart label reads at 17 px. The card keeps the source line and names Oath & Action and the atlas; it carries no web address until the site is settled.

Studio note for reviewers

Social card · built from S01

What changes. The switch, the downloads and the readout drop. The title, measure, figure and source stay. The table travels as the alt text.

Size. 1080 by 1350 px, the portrait post for Instagram and LinkedIn; 64 px margins on the 8 px rhythm.

Kit. social_card() measures the title, measure and source, then asks the generator for the narrowest artboard that fills the card’s 952 px width and fits the height left over. A module whose scale would fall under 1.3 times stops the build until its title or artboard is shorter.

Chart system · Concept 03 · System

The kit on one sheet

The reading guide first, then what a builder needs to make the next chart without asking: the module’s seven slots, its sizes, the type ramp, the marks, the codes, the palettes with measured contrast, the red rule, the annotation and source rules, the generators and what changes between a still image and a panel.

01 How to read our charts

For readers. Every chart’s source line links here, and this list can run on the atlas’s help page and under a report’s first chart.

  1. What kind of claim. The small label above the title says what kind of claim the chart makes. A Finding reports what the data shows: a count, a measured rate or a record. An Association says two things move together and does not say one causes the other. An Estimate says what would or may happen if stated assumptions hold. An Illustration explains an idea with an example; its numbers are made up and labeled so.
  2. How sure. After the kind come a few words on the evidence: documented means on the public record; an official statistic comes from a government survey or count; a secondary source is someone else’s list that Oath & Action checked against its own record.
  3. The verb in the title. The verb matches the evidence. Documented facts take plain record words: was, passed, logged. A strong research finding says raises or lowers. Some evidence says can or may. Disputed evidence gives both readings. An untested idea says untested. A scenario says would or may.
  4. The line under the title. It names what was measured, where and when, and says when a scale does not start at zero.
  5. Dark and gray. The darkest mark is the one the title is about; gray marks are there for comparison. Where a chart uses a code of its own, such as the grades, its key says so.
  6. Red. A red mark, when a chart has one, points at the single thing the title names. It never marks a party or a side, and it carries no verdict on either.
  7. Texture. In the evidence charts, solid means documented or well supported, a light tint means plausible, and a hatch means contested, as solid, dashed and dash-dot lines do on the atlas.
  8. Survey numbers. Survey numbers come from a sample of people, so each has a margin of error. A margin of 0.5 points means the true figure most likely sits within half a point either way, and a smaller change may be chance. When a table publishes no margin, a change of a point or two prints as little changed.
  9. Records. Codes such as RL07 or PW15 in a chart’s top line are record numbers. Search the atlas for them to read the full record.
  10. Check it. Every chart has a Table button, and its source sits under it in both states. The downloads give you the same numbers.

02 The module

One chart, every part named. The letters in the margin match the table.

The seven slots
SlotHoldsTypeSpace above, px
A IndexThe evidence kind and its grade in words at left; the atlas record index at right, when the chart has oneKind Inter 700, 13/18, +0.060 em, capitals; grade Inter 400, 13/18; index Inter 600, 13/18, Deep Stone2 px Charcoal rule, then 12
B TitleOne sentence that states the finding, its verb matched to the gradeInter Tight 800, 28/32, −0.025 em; Inter Tight 800, 22/26, −0.020 em on phones8
C MeasureMeasure, unit, place and period; where a scale starts if not at zeroInter 400, 15/23, Deep Stone, 38 em at most8
D ControlsChart and Table switch at left, downloads at right. Panel onlyInter 600, 14; 32 px targets, 44 on phones16
E FigureOne artboard at the module’s width, its notes inside the drawing; or an HTML table or grid that reflowsLabels Inter 600, 13/16; notes Inter 400, 13/1616
F NotesWhat a reader needs to read the chart honestly: coding rules, qualifications, the disclosureInter 400, 14/20, 36 em at most (45 to 75 characters)16
G SourceSource line in section 15 order; the credit and the reading guide link at right; then a 1 px Stone ruleInter 400, 13/18, Deep Stone12, then 16 below

A slot never moves and never changes job. An empty slot closes up, except B, C, E and G, which every chart fills. The figure slot holds one artboard at a time: a container query shows the widest artboard that fits the module, so a drawing is never scaled up or down and every line stays in the 1, 1.5, 2, 3 and 6 px family.

03 Sizes and spacing

Widths

  • Column module, 866 px. 8 of 12 columns at 1440; the default for atlas pages and reports
  • Still, 680 px. Substack and email body; exported at 2x
  • Social card artboard, 600 px. Chosen by social_card() and set at 1.34x inside the 1080 by 1350 card
  • Medium artboard, 560 px. Tablets and narrow windows
  • Phone artboard, 390, 358 px. Drawn at 358, the column of a 390 px phone
  • Phone artboard, 360, 328 px. Drawn at 328, the column of a 360 px phone

Spacing

Every gap is a step of the Signal Grid’s 8 px rhythm, with its 4 px half step. Modules stack 72 px apart; slots sit 8 to 16 px apart; rows in a chart sit on 32 to 40 px.

Figures are tabular only where they are figures, so a hyphen inside a word keeps its own width. Lora Italic sets quoted words inside a note and nothing else; no chart title or label uses a serif. On Charcoal, text from 13 to 15 px sets one weight heavier.

05 Marks

Line weights

  • 1 px. Hairline: gridlines, leaders, rules and the bar track, on half pixels so a 1x export prints them crisp
  • 1.5 px. Context lines in small multiples; the open ring for an earlier year; outlines
  • 2 px. Context series in a line chart; the threshold tick; dumbbell connectors
  • 3 px. The series the title names; the red point mark
  • 6 px. The lit selection in an interactive panel only

Marks

  • Units: 24 px squares 4 px apart, one per record. A roll-up record draws as a stack three units wide and says what it holds.
  • Ranked bars: 24 px tall on a 40 px pitch; counts inside when the segment is 18 px or wider. 100% bars: 18 px on a 36 px pitch.
  • Dots: 6 px radius for the later year, a 5 px open ring for the earlier; 5 px on a timeline; 4 px where a note points.

06 Codes after color

Every code survives grayscale through a second channel: fill against outline, texture, shape or position.

Direction code, repair log

  • Away from voters. Solid Charcoal.
  • Toward voters. Verdigris strong with an inner frame in the ground color: the frame sets it apart from away on any copy.
  • Kept existing rules. Light fill with a Stone outline.
  • Mixed. Split: both fills in one mark.
  • Pending. Open: an outline on the ground, for a change still undecided.

Grayscale holds the order: Charcoal, Verdigris strong with its frame, Stone light, ground. Rows in S08 and segment order in S03 add a third code.

Scenario arrows

  • Up.
  • Slightly up.
  • Flat.
  • Flat or down.
  • Down.
  • Mixed.
  • Same as scenario ii.

The arrow in its box carries the direction on a black-and-white copy; a Verdigris or Prussian tint carries the side as a second code. No scale pairs red with blue. Party marks take neutral inks with the party’s name printed on them, ordered by value or alphabet.

Evidence grades: one table for every V7 label

Evidence grades
Display wordV7 keyReader’s meaningFill, in this orderLine on the atlasTitle verb
Documenteddocumentedon the public record Solid, the darkest ink solidrecord language: was, passed, logged
Well supportedwell-supportedstrong research evidence Solid, a gray step lighter solida direct finding: raises, lowers
Plausibleplausiblesome evidence Light solid tint with an outline dashed“can” or “may”
Contestedcontestedevidence disputed Diagonal hatch with an outline dash-dotboth readings, side by side
Hypothesishypothesisuntested Dots with an outline dotted“untested”

The code covers claims and connections alike. V7’s key plausible_contested prints as Contested. Grades never take red. Where a chart’s categories carry their own code, as grades do, rank the rows by the code’s order or draw every bar in one ink and print the grade, so the darkest-ink rule never points at a grade by accident.

Contrast is WCAG 2 against the ground, computed by the build script. Every tint is one of the palette lab’s OKLab mixes of locked colors; the script recovered each mix and prints it above. Kept existing rules, the plausible tint, the up and down tints and the gridline fall under 3:1 by design: each kept segment prints its count and carries a Stone outline, each plausible segment carries an outline, each tinted cell prints the atlas’s words beside an arrow, and gridlines carry no meaning. Pillar Red appears in the table as a swatch, which Rule 05.3 does not count.

08 Red

The wordmark’s ampersand and the lockmark’s lever are signature red and do not count, and neither do the ampersands inside the hinge diagram and the hinge-circle badge, which are identity marks. The hinge diagram never shares a view with the wordmark and never stands in for the hinge divider. An icon’s red accent counts as signature red when the icon stands alone, as an app tile, an avatar or a single feature icon. In a row or a menu, icons go one color and only the current one keeps its red. Each view (one screen, card, slide or printed page) then carries one working red, in this order of precedence: an error the reader must fix; the step a reader can take now; the one point the headline names, which in a systems figure is where a reform acts. One job may take several marks, such as each target of one reform. A hinge headline’s ampersand uses the view’s working red. The hinge divider’s ampersand takes its surface’s ink: Charcoal on Newsprint and White, Newsprint on Charcoal, White on Prussian. In the guide itself, specimens, labeled failure cases and palette swatches do not count. Red never sits on Prussian.

Rule 05.3, the red rule (D2-01)

On a chart page each module counts as one view. Red never codes a series, a category, a scale, a party or a grade. It may mark the one point a title names, here the 7 votes the Senate fell short in S01, and only when no error or ask holds the view. Press the button to put an ask in this view: the ask takes the red, and the shortfall steps down to Charcoal at the same 3 px weight.

A chart on its own, or added to a page. A chart posted alone, as a card or a still, may mark the point its title names in red. A chart added to a page takes red only when the page’s red job moves to it.

See how each senator votedIllustrative ask

09 Annotation, sources and reader words

  1. Notes sit inside the drawing when they are short. Inter 13 in Deep Stone, joined to the data by 1 px leaders, clear of every gridline or on a band in the ground color. Long notes go in the notes slot, where they wrap at 45 to 75 characters a line.
  2. Label directly. Labels sit on the mark or at its end. A key appears only when labels cannot fit, and it sits inside the drawing above the marks it explains.
  3. Write the unit once. On the top tick or the first label: “100%”, “17 changes”, “Down 3.7 points”. Other ticks stay bare.
  4. Numbers are tabular, and minus is the true minus. Write −3.7 with U+2212. Dates print in words with no line break inside them.
  5. Scales are honest. Bars start at zero. A line or dot scale may start elsewhere when the measure line says so. Small multiples share one scale. Missing years and method breaks stay open; no line joins them.
  6. Small changes are changes. A change of a point or two in a survey with no published margin of error prints as “little changed”, never as a fall or a rise.
  7. Hover repeats the table. The readout under a chart repeats what the table holds. Every value is printed, in the notes or in the table.
  8. The source line goes under every chart. In section 15 order: publisher, title or table, observation period, geography, date retrieved, qualification. Shorten by dropping words; every fact stays. The credit and the link to the reading guide sit at the right.
  9. Record IDs stay in the index and the tables. RL07, PW15 and E09 print in slot A and in the table, where a reader looks a record up, and nowhere on the face of a drawing. When a dataset mixes ID prefixes, the index prints the count and the prefixes: “118 connections, IDs L, LE, LT, LX and T”.
  10. No reader sees studio words. No color names, source codes or “the studio” on the face of a chart or in its notes; say “the dark line”, “the gray bars”, “Oath & Action”.
  11. Read every title twice. Before a title ships, read it once as a reader on the left and once as a reader on the right. If either would take it as a side, rewrite it.
  12. Disclose where the editor works on the subject. Charts on nomination, ranked-ballot or election-rule data print the editor’s disclosure in the notes, labeled “Disclosure:”.
  13. Illustrative items carry the word. “Illustrative data” or “Illustrative ask” sits beside the item itself.

10 The kit

A chart joins the kit with one call to register_chart(): its dataset, its generator, an adapter that reads the shared data into a spec, a table builder for the equivalent and the CSV columns. The module then supplies all seven slots, the Chart and Table switch, both downloads, the still and the coverage check. Every generator draws through Art, which measures each label with the Inter files in ./fonts and stops the build when a label leaves its drawing, touches another, or meets a line, rule, leader or mark, with 15% headroom for wider text spacing.

Generators and their inputs
GeneratorSpec it readsUsed by
big_number(art, spec)figure, group_head, groups (key, label, value, party, context), vote_head, votes (label, sub, scale, segs, threshold, red)S01
line_events(art, spec)x_range, x_ticks, y_max, y_step, series (segments of points, line and dot classes), breaks (x, word, top), labels per layout, notes (point, text, side)S02
ranked_bar(art, spec)rows (key, label, total, segs of field, value and code, note, sub), key, unit; the scale comes from the largest totalS03
dumbbell(art, spec)rows (label, a and b points, change words, context), years; the scale crops to whole tens around the dataS04
small_multiples(art, spec)panels (id, name, segments, last, note), y_range, x_range, note_atS05
comparison_table(uid, spec)rows with the atlas’s words and a class per family, families, key_head, captionS06
tile_map(art, spec)tiles (col, row, key, status, fill, year, tip), key, size_note; the grid comes from geo/us-state-tile-grid.jsonS07
unit_ledger(uid, spec)rows (code, word, records), rollups (key: label and tip), labelS08
strip_timeline(art, spec)lanes (label, question, events with exact fractional dates), x_range, ticksS09
share_bars(art, spec)rows (key, label, total, segs of grade and count), grades, unit, share_field, right_headS10

A worked example

register_chart('X01', 'link-grades', share_bars, adapter=spec_x01, table=eq_x01,
               csv_cols=['key', 'documented', 'well-supported', 'plausible', 'contested', 'hypothesis'])

def spec_x01():
    return {'kind_words': ..., 'title': ..., 'measure': [...], 'index': '118 connections, IDs L, LE, LT, LX and T',
            'rows': [...], 'grades': [...], 'unit': 'links', 'share_field': 'documented', 'right_head': 'Documented',
            'notes': [...], 'drawn': [...], 'label': ..., 'why': ...}

Downloads name their files YYYYMMDD_Oath-And-Action-<ID>-<Dataset-Title>; the SVG carries the chart’s title and alt text as <title> and <desc>. The SVG names its fonts and carries no font files, so a design tool needs Inter and Inter Tight installed. A PNG still would come from an export step the kit does not build yet. Motion is not in the kit yet; the first animated chart arrives with a reduced-motion path that shows the final state.

11 Still image and interactive panel

Still and panel

  • Stays. Slots A, B, C, E, F and G in the same order and the same type; every printed number; every note; the source line.
  • Drops. Slot D: the Chart and Table switch and the downloads. The tap and hover readout.
  • Adds. Alt text with every value and the source, sent with the image, and a line in the notes that says where the table and data live.
  • Changes. The figure uses a 680 px artboard drawn by the same generator and exports at 2x for Substack and email. Nothing moves between slots.
